notes: I4 is the deciding and borderline criterion. The only surface-area statement in the main text (no supplementary files were provided) is the sentence quoted under I4, about Norit Darco G-60. It describes what this type of carbon 'generally' has, gives no method, and is not tied to a measurement on the sample used. The same sentence says it has an area 'approximately 70 times larger than the VGCF [10]', with [10] a citation to earlier work. No other sample has an area, and a text search for area, BET, Langmuir and pore found nothing else; Table 1 lists no areas. I read this as no specific surface area reported for any measured sample. If a resolver counts the generic ~700 m2/g as a reported area for G-60, I4 would be met (method unspecified, same-sample status unclear) and the paper would be eligible, since I1, I2, I3 and I5 are met. I1: original volumetric uptake on a commercial Gas Reaction Controller (PCI system), and a manual high-pressure system gives upper limits only; the uptakes are tiny (all carbon values below 0.1 wt.% in the PCI column). Table 1 gives 23°C, and Fig. 14 gives 25°C for the FeNiCu filaments. Table 1 lists 3.59 MPa for the PCI column and 11 MPa for the manual column.
